chapter.title: VOLUME ONE: NAME THAT CHORD
chapter.summary: A systematic catalog of tertian sonorities — triads, seventh chords, and TBN (Two-Note Base) constructs — in both Close and Spread voicings, organized across six cycles (2–7) and three parent scales (C Major, C Melodic Minor, C Harmonic Minor). The book's teaching is encoded entirely in tabular mappings across three analytical layers: Intervallic Voice-Leading, Functional Voice-Leading, and M.S.R.P. No instructional prose is present; the catalog itself is the argument.

sections.title: Cycle × Scale Grid — 18 Environments
sections.summary: The master organizational axis of Volume One: every voicing entry is located at the intersection of one of six cycles (2–7, representing the interval of root motion) and one of three parent scales (C Major, C Melodic Minor, C Harmonic Minor), producing 18 distinct voice-leading environments per voicing family.

engine_rules.name: Locate Voicing Entry at Cycle × Scale Intersection

then.voicing.scale_context: constrain all voice-leading analysis to the parent scale of the cell

engine_rules.falsifier: A voicing entry that produces valid output when cycle.id or scale.context is unspecified
engine_rules.anchor: six cycles (2-7) within three parent scales: C Major, C Melodic Minor, and C Harmonic Minor

engine_rules.name: Cycle Number Is Root-Motion Interval

then.voicing.cycle_index: root moves by interval N where N equals cycle number

engine_rules.falsifier: A cycle labeled cycle-4 that produces root motion by an interval other than a fourth
engine_rules.anchor: cycles (cycles 2 through 7, representing the interval of motion between successive diatonic chords)

engine_rules.name: Cycle and Scale Are Orthogonal Traversal Axes

then.voicing.cycle_index: cycle axis may be varied independently of scale axis
then.voicing.scale_context: scale axis may be varied independently of cycle axis

engine_rules.falsifier: Any (cycle, scale) cell found to be empty
engine_rules.anchor: six cycles × 3 parent scales produces 18 distinct voice-leading environments

sections.title: Close and Spread Position Parameterization
sections.summary: Every voicing family is cataloged in both Close and Spread positions, treated as independent objects with separate voice-leading tables. This parameterizes voicing density as an axis orthogonal to cycle and scale.

engine_rules.name: Close and Spread Are Independent Voice-Leading Objects

then.voicing.shape: select the voice-leading table specific to voicing.position

engine_rules.falsifier: A case where Close and Spread entries produce identical intervallic voice-leading profiles
engine_rules.anchor: Each voicing is displayed in both close and spread positions

engine_rules.name: Position Choice Reshapes Contrapuntal Texture Without Changing Harmonic Content

then.voicing.shape: toggle between close and spread to modify contrapuntal texture; harmonic content preserved

engine_rules.falsifier: A position toggle that changes the pitch-class set
engine_rules.anchor: the guitarist can trace how register choice reshapes the contrapuntal texture without changing the harmonic content

sections.title: Three-Layer Analytical Method
sections.summary: Every voicing entry is analyzed through three mandatory lenses: Intervallic Voice-Leading, Functional Voice-Leading, M.S.R.P.

engine_rules.name: Read Intervallic Layer First to Establish Motion Budget

then.voicing.cycle_index: identify common tone, step voices, leap voices

engine_rules.falsifier: A voicing selection that contradicts the intervallic profile listed
engine_rules.anchor: intervallic voice-leading relationships

engine_rules.name: Functional Layer Tracks Scale-Degree Role Across Cycle Steps

then.voicing.functional_class: assign each voice a scale-degree function and track which function moves to which

engine_rules.falsifier: An entry where two voices carry the same scale-degree function within the same chord
engine_rules.anchor: functional voice-leading information

engine_rules.name: M.S.R.P. Selects Most Stepwise Top-Voice Path Through Cycle

then.voicing.msrp: prefer voicing sequence whose top voice matches M.S.R.P. encoding

engine_rules.falsifier: A voicing path preferred over M.S.R.P. despite producing less stepwise top-voice
engine_rules.anchor: Most Stepwise Resolution Pattern (M.S.R.P.) strings

engine_rules.name: Prefer the Voice That Carries the Common Tone to Sustain or Minimally Move

then.voicing.cycle_index: hold or minimally displace common-tone voice across cycle step

engine_rules.falsifier: A cycle environment where no voice carries interval 0
engine_rules.anchor: intervallic voice-leading relationships, functional voice-leading information

engine_rules.name: Identical Functional Voice-Leading Profiles Signal Substitution Equivalence
engine_rules.falsifier: Two entries with identical functional profiles that produce non-substitutable results
engine_rules.anchor: functional voice-leading information

sections.title: Tertian Voicing Families — Triads and Seventh Chords
sections.summary: Triads (3-voice) and seventh chords (4-voice), each cataloged across all 18 environments in both Close and Spread positions.

engine_rules.name: Triad Entries Are 3-Voice Objects in Both Close and Spread
engine_rules.falsifier: A triad entry with fewer than 3 or more than 3 distinct voices
engine_rules.anchor: triads, seventh chords, and Goodrick's TBN (Two-Note Base) constructs — in both Close and Spread voicings

engine_rules.name: Seventh Chord Entries Are 4-Voice Objects in Both Close and Spread
engine_rules.falsifier: A seventh-chord entry with fewer than 4 or more than 4 distinct voices
engine_rules.anchor: triads, seventh chords, and Goodrick's TBN (Two-Note Base) constructs — in both Close and Spread voicings

engine_rules.name: Common-Tone-Rich Cycles Yield Smoother Voice-Leading Automatically

then.voicing.cycle_index: expect one or more common tones per cycle step
then.voicing.msrp: M.S.R.P. reflects predominantly stepwise or common-tone top-voice motion

engine_rules.falsifier: A cycle-4 or cycle-5 cell where no voice carries interval 0
engine_rules.anchor: some cycles (particularly cycles producing common-tone-rich motion) yield smooth voice-leading almost automatically

sections.title: TBN (Two-Note Base) Constructs
sections.summary: Goodrick's TBN constructs — Two-Note Base Type I and Type II — extend the tertian catalog by pairing a two-note interval base with upper structure voices.

engine_rules.name: TBN Constructs Receive All Three Analytical Layers Identically

then.voicing.cycle_index: apply intervallic layer to TBN base and upper structure
then.voicing.functional_class: assign functional labels to TBN voices
then.voicing.msrp: read M.S.R.P. string identically to tertian procedure

engine_rules.falsifier: A TBN entry that omits one of the three analytical layers
engine_rules.anchor: triads, seventh chords, and Goodrick's TBN (Two-Note Base) constructs

chapter.title: VOLUME TWO: DO NOT NAME THAT CHORD
chapter.summary: Applies the identical analytical framework of Volume One to quartal and cluster sonorities — 3-part quartal, 4-part quartal (six voicing types), and Spread Cluster (six voicing types) — across the same 18-environment grid.

sections.title: Quartal / Cluster Catalog — Same Grid, Different Primitives
sections.summary: Volume Two applies the 18-environment grid to quartal and cluster sonorities.

engine_rules.name: Quartal and Cluster Voicings Use the Same 18-Environment Grid as Tertian
engine_rules.falsifier: A quartal or cluster entry outside the 18-environment grid
engine_rules.anchor: six cycles (cycles 2-7) and three parent scales (C Major, C Melodic Minor, and C Harmonic Minor)

engine_rules.name: Quartal and Cluster Entries Receive All Three Analytical Layers
engine_rules.falsifier: A quartal or cluster entry that lacks one of the three layers
engine_rules.anchor: Intervallic Voice-Leading (pitch relationships), Functional Voice-Leading (harmonic context)

engine_rules.name: Quartal and Cluster Voicings Are Applied Without Requiring a Chord Name

when.chord_quality: ambiguous or unnameable by tertian convention

then.voicing.functional_class: do not force a tertian chord-quality label

engine_rules.preference: required when chord_quality cannot be resolved
engine_rules.falsifier: A quartal or cluster entry defined only in relation to an underlying tertian chord name
engine_rules.anchor: the volume's strategic shift away from tertian harmony toward quartal and cluster sonorities that resist conventional chord naming

engine_rules.name: 4-Part Quartal Has Six Distinct Voicing Types

then.voicing.shape: select one of six 4-part quartal voicing types

engine_rules.falsifier: Fewer than or more than six distinct 4-part quartal voicing types
engine_rules.anchor: 4-part quartal voicings across six distinct voicing types

engine_rules.name: Spread Cluster Has Six Distinct Voicing Types

then.voicing.shape: select one of six Spread Cluster voicing types

engine_rules.falsifier: Fewer than or more than six distinct Spread Cluster voicing types
engine_rules.anchor: Spread Cluster voicings across six further types

sections.title: Unity of Voice-Leading Across Families
sections.summary: By running every non-tertian voicing family through the same 18-environment grid, the Almanac proves voice-leading discipline is invariant across families.

engine_rules.name: Voice-Leading Discipline Is Invariant Across Sonority Families

then.voicing.cycle_index: apply same motion-budget analysis regardless of family
then.voicing.functional_class: track scale-degree or quartal-equivalent function using same logic

engine_rules.falsifier: A voicing family requiring a fourth analytical layer or different grid
engine_rules.anchor: quartal and cluster harmony is not a special case requiring special treatment. It obeys the same voice-leading discipline as tertian harmony

engine_rules.name: Switching Voicing Family Does Not Change Motion-Budget Reading Procedure

then.voicing.cycle_index: read intervallic layer using same procedure regardless of family

engine_rules.falsifier: A quartal or cluster entry where interval 0 cannot be identified using the same procedure
engine_rules.anchor: By running 4-part fourths and spread cluster voicings through the same 18-environment grid, with the same three analytical layers, Goodrick enforces the insight that the guitarist's contrapuntal obligation does not change when the harmonic language does

engine_rules.name: Families With Fewer Common Tones Per Cycle Force Larger Leap Budgets

then.voicing.cycle_index: expect larger or more frequent intervallic leaps

engine_rules.anchor: What changes across families is which voice carries the common tone, which voice steps by a second or third, and how large the remaining leaps must be

engine_rules.name: M.S.R.P. Is the Top-Voice Efficiency Benchmark for Quartal and Cluster Cycles

then.voicing.msrp: use M.S.R.P. string as compact melodic handle on multi-voice contrapuntal event

engine_rules.falsifier: A quartal or cluster entry where M.S.R.P. string is absent while equivalent tertian entry at same address has valid M.S.R.P.
engine_rules.anchor: M.S.R.P. string indicating the Most Stepwise Resolution Pattern
